title: Esgridge's POEMS work at Marshall and Alzofon's nucleonic spin

tellings.quote: something that Richard Esgridge looked into at Marshall and then uh Alzafon's nucleonic spin approaches that he sort of scrubbed with Fineman back in the 30s.

plain: Ideas for unusual propulsion physics have a long history, according to Jack, Michels' co-host, who uses a pseudonym and says he works in sensitive defense areas. He points to work by Richard Esgridge at NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center, done under a program known as POEMS (an acronym he does not spell out), and to "nucleonic spin approaches" by a scientist named Alzofon, which Jack says Alzofon went over with the physicist Richard Feynman in the 1930s. He gives no source. If true, it would mean this line of research was being explored decades before today's debates over such technology.
